media.narrative_summary: This video is a Turkish-language explainer about 'mini-AGI,' an open-source continual learning language model hosted on GitHub by user 'volotat.' It opens by showing a terminal log indicating '397 experts' and asks how many the model accumulated. The narrator describes mini-AGI as a model trained from scratch on an 8GB VRAM laptop with batch-1 streaming data, released under an MIT license, and having approximately 1,300 stars. Because the full model does not fit in memory, its weights are stored on disk and paged into RAM and VRAM as needed while the model reads — the expert pool grows automatically during training. According to the README, the model has 1.257 billion total parameters, but only about 109 million reside on the GPU at once. In a forgetting test, it retained 97.30% of prior knowledge. The creator notes three caveats: it is still at a 'toy' level, final weights have not been published yet, and running it requires weeks of GPU training. The video ends by encouraging viewers to save the repository and share it with a friend.
